reviews.body: Reviewed at head 4dd46fce (static review). The fix is correctly placed: filtering runs before every early return (image-only pass-through, upload marker, already-framed), so the untyped bare-string parts can no longer survive any of the paths #8037 identified. The predicate (`not block`) matches `_extract_text_from_content`'s skip exactly, all-empty lists collapse to `""` as documented, and the returned copies are built from `deepcopy` so the persisted message stays untouched (asserted). Coverage looks right: five insertion positions around typed/bare/image blocks plus image-only / upload / framed / all-empty shapes across sync and async, and the middlewares AGENTS.md is updated. Three non-blocking findings below; none block this fix.

review_comments.body: **Important (residual path, same crash class):** when `original_user_content` is set and `rfind` fails (the extraction-disagreement branch around lines 387-407), the per-block fallback does `new_content.append(frame_untrusted_text(block))` — a bare string stays a bare string in the outgoing content list. A non-empty bare string there still reaches the provider as an untyped content part, i.e. exactly the Chat Completions 400 this PR removes everywhere else. Wrapping the framed result as `{"type": "text", "text": ...}` in that branch would close the class. Pre-existing and only reachable on the disagreement path, so fine to defer — but worth a follow-up issue or a sentence in the AGENTS.md note added here.

**Suggestion (scope of the predicate):** this removes empty *bare* strings only. `_extract_text_from_content` skips empty typed text blocks symmetrically (`{"type": "text", "text": ""}` — line 295, same "matches message_content_to_text behaviour" comment), but those still survive every path here: extraction skips them and `_rebuild_content` treats them as non-text blocks and re-inserts them (e.g. `["", {"type": "text", "text": ""}, {"type": "text", "text": "hi"}]` → `[{"type": "text", "text": ""}, merged-text]`). Chat Completions accepts typed empty parts, but Anthropic rejects empty text blocks, so the request can still 400 there. If provider-safe content is the goal, consider extending the filter to empty typed text blocks too — or noting in the AGENTS.md paragraph why they intentionally stay.

**Nit / question on the all-empty shape:** `["", ""]` → content `""`. OpenAI accepts empty string user content, but Anthropic turns string content into a text block and rejects empty text, so an all-empty turn can still 400 on Anthropic-backed runs. Since this middleware replaces messages in place and cannot drop them, `""` is the reasonable local choice — but is an all-empty-turn drop (or placeholder) handled anywhere upstream (Gateway / IM channels)? If not, worth a line in the PR body or the AGENTS.md note acknowledging the residual case.

comments.body:
The middleware AGENTS.md now records all three residual cases. The upload
extraction-disagreement fallback can retain non-empty untyped strings; empty
typed text blocks are outside this fix's empty-bare-string scope; and collapsing
an all-empty list to an empty string does not guarantee Anthropic acceptance.
No upstream Gateway / IM empty-turn handling is assumed. The affected middleware
suite still passes all 225 tests.
